examples.title: Air-cored solenoid: complete magnetostatic tutorial
examples.summary: Construct and solve an air-cored solenoid in r/z coordinates, with explicitly assigned winding, air and open-boundary regions; inspect fields and circuit properties.
assumptions: The source is a FEMM 4.2 tutorial with a steady 1 A excitation and explicitly specified turns/dimensions.
limitations: Legacy platform instructions are historical; operation compatibility must be checked for the chosen FEMM build.

examples.title: Gapped EI inductor: linkage and energy inductance
examples.summary: Compare a planar gapped EI-core inductor with magnetic-circuit theory, then cross-check circuit flux-linkage and stored-energy estimates of inductance.
assumptions: The source assumes constant relative permeability and an explicit planar depth.
The single winding and absence of permanent magnets permit the linear self-inductance identities.
limitations: Fringing and leakage make the magnetic-circuit estimate approximate.
An open-boundary formulation can require additional care in an energy comparison.

examples.title: Gapped EI inductor: DC and harmonic force
examples.summary: Reuse the EI geometry while comparing DC force with harmonic mean and twice-frequency force under an explicit peak-current convention.
assumptions: The source compares linear DC and 60 Hz cases using peak phasors.
limitations: Its half-DC mean-force result depends on the stated linear excitation assumptions.

examples.title: Planar bar magnet: material and orientation
examples.summary: Define a rectangular N42 magnet, assign magnetization direction and an exterior air/IABC region, then inspect flux lines and field magnitude.
assumptions: The physical bar is approximated by its specified planar cross-section and depth.
limitations: A material-library name alone is not a complete magnet definition.
The reconstructed rectangle preview does not include all magnet properties or the exterior region.

examples.title: Two magnets and steel bar: IABC open domain
examples.summary: Use the open-boundary builder on a magnet-and-steel assembly, recording shell count, center, radius and Dirichlet/Neumann outer-edge choice.
assumptions: The source uses specified permanent magnets and 1018 steel.
limitations: The IABC order and distance are numerical choices, not universal constants.

examples.title: Tapered plunger: force over stroke
examples.summary: Move the complete tapered plunger group through a stroke, solve at each position, and compare weighted-stress force with the experimental curve cited by the source.
assumptions: The source defines a B-H curve from Roters and keeps the coil excitation fixed.
limitations: Published curve digitization and agreement are source evidence, not fresh library validation.
Static force snapshots do not by themselves simulate motion.

examples.title: Conducting steel tube: induced current benchmark
examples.summary: Model a sinusoidal-current wire inside a finite isolated conductive steel tube, enforce zero net tube current and compare radial current-density profiles with the analytical Bessel-function solution.
assumptions: Linear permeability/conductivity and a finite-tube net-current constraint are stated explicitly.
limitations: The zero-net-current condition is different from an externally driven or grounded-at-infinity tube.
Analytical agreement reported by the source has not been rerun here.

examples.title: TEAM 28: steady levitation of an aluminum plate
examples.summary: Analyze stationary concentric coils and a conducting plate at the published steady levitation condition, comparing asymptotic and Kelvin open-boundary treatments.
assumptions: This example addresses steady-state levitation, not the full transient TEAM problem.
The source supplies coil current and a bulk winding approximation.
limitations: The two exterior treatments are alternatives with different implementation details.
Equilibrium height requires comparison with the mechanical load.

examples.title: Woofer motor: BL, resistance and incremental inductance
examples.summary: Group and translate the voice coil in a permanent-magnet speaker motor; extract force factor, DC winding properties and finite-difference incremental inductance about magnet bias.
assumptions: The source models an axisymmetric woofer and uses grouped coil motion.
limitations: Total magnet-biased linkage divided by current is not incremental self-inductance.
The source geometry is an example rather than a production-device certification.

examples.title: Parameterized air-core coil inductance and Wheeler comparison
examples.summary: Programmatically construct an arbitrary cylindrical air-core winding, solve at one ampere, read circuit linkage and compare selected dimensions with the applicable empirical Wheeler formula.
assumptions: The source Octave function uses inches and an explicit one-ampere circuit.
limitations: The empirical formula has its own geometry applicability and is not an exact reference.

examples.title: Iron ball and coil: batch force-position curve
examples.summary: Use an existing grouped iron-ball/coil geometry in a scripted position sweep, with Kelvin exterior mapping and weighted-stress force extraction.
assumptions: Current density and source winding conventions remain fixed during the source sweep.
limitations: A static force-position calculation is not a transient launcher model.

examples.title: Single-phase transformer operating point under load
examples.summary: Iterate current-driven FEMM solutions with an external impedance-matrix update until prescribed primary voltage and secondary load conditions are met.
assumptions: The source neglects selected joint gaps, rolling-direction and end-turn impedance effects.
FEMM materials account for the particular included core/winding loss approximations.
limitations: The approximate iteration matrix and nonlinear operating regime affect convergence.

examples.title: Custom element-by-element magnetic energy integral
examples.summary: Compare raw element-centroid integration of linear magnetic energy with the built-in group energy integral, using explicit element areas and planar depth conversion.
assumptions: The selected region is magnetically linear and smoothing is disabled for the custom element calculation.
limitations: A planar depth-weighted formula must be changed for axisymmetric volume weighting.

examples.title: Historical filelink client protocol
examples.summary: Document the source client that exchanges command/result text through temporary files with a FEMM executable launched in filelink mode.
assumptions: The example describes the historical FEMM 4.x Windows filelink interface.
limitations: It is not the native FEMM 5 communication protocol.
The demonstrated polling and input parsing need independent hardening before operational reuse.

examples.title: Historical out-of-process ActiveX client
examples.summary: Document creation of an ActiveX client, command dispatch and result/error parsing through the historical FEMM COM server.
assumptions: The example uses MSVC++ type-library bindings and a Windows ActiveX server.
limitations: Its binding assumptions do not transfer directly to Linux-native FEMM 5.

examples.title: Round-wire winding skin and proximity continuum model
examples.summary: Compare explicit-wire modeling with the version-specific bulk constitutive winding model used to represent skin/proximity effects economically.
assumptions: Equivalent properties are based on the documented packed-round-wire approximation.
limitations: High-frequency and extreme-fill behavior depends on the particular approximation/version.

examples.title: Aluminum cylinder: boundary-temperature transient
examples.summary: Start from a steady initial temperature and step the aluminum cylinder thermal solution after the external boundary temperature changes, preserving the mesh across time steps.
assumptions: The source models an axisymmetric aluminum cylinder and uses implicit Euler steps.
limitations: A fixed mesh is required by the documented transient implementation.
Time-step accuracy needs a separate refinement study.

examples.title: Historical multi-instance OctaveFEMM routing
examples.summary: Keep distinct handles for two FEMM servers and explicitly select the intended handle before each sequence of commands and shutdown.
assumptions: The example exposes the legacy OctaveFEMM global HandleToFEMM.
limitations: A shared global handle is not a thread-local connection model.
Modern TCP session selection must follow its own binding contract.

examples.title: Default block material in otherwise unlabeled regions
examples.summary: Attach a default flag to a valid material label and observe its effect on otherwise unlabeled circular regions while retaining the documented mesh-size limitation.
assumptions: The described implementation is available in the cited FEMM 4.2 build and has analogous other-physics commands.
limitations: The default material must be valid; its mesh-size setting is not enforced in unlabeled regions.

examples.title: Cone/sphere electrostatics: meshing and energy convergence
examples.summary: Use the sharp cone/sphere stored-energy benchmark to compare historical meshing heuristics and a succession of refined meshes.
assumptions: The source fixes physical electrode geometry and voltage while varying numerical mesh resolution.
limitations: Historical Triangle heuristics and exact source node counts are not guarantees for the current FEMM 5 mesher.
A converged energy integral does not imply every local field is converged.

examples.title: Long-stator eddy-current brake: force versus speed
examples.summary: Map plate speed to apparent AC frequency for a fundamental travelling current source, then compute the mean braking-force curve with the source edge-effect approximations.
assumptions: The source keeps one periodic wavelength and uses approximate transverse fringing/conductivity corrections.
limitations: Higher spatial harmonics and significant short-stator end effects require a richer model.

examples.title: Speaker blocked impedance over frequency and position
examples.summary: Solve a magnet-biased DC operating point at each coil position, then evaluate incremental AC impedance and inductance across a frequency range.
assumptions: Small-signal AC response is linearized about the matching DC operating point.
limitations: It is not a full coupled transient loudspeaker solution.
Surface mesh requirements depend on frequency, conductivity and incremental permeability.

examples.title: Speaker at 1 kHz: position sweep with and without a ring
examples.summary: Compare coil impedance, inductance and BL across positions at 1 kHz for matched source geometries with and without a copper shorting ring.
assumptions: The source uses a lower maximum frequency than the broad blocked-impedance study.
limitations: The coarser source mesh is a frequency/material-specific choice.
The ring and no-ring variants are distinct physical configurations.

examples.title: Speaker transient model from identified impedance maps
examples.summary: Fit a position-dependent multi-section L/R network to FEMM impedance maps and combine it with external mechanical dynamics to calculate a speaker transient.
assumptions: Field-derived maps and published mechanical parameters are combined by an external system model.
limitations: The source prototype-inspired geometry is not asserted to represent the production loudspeaker.
FEMM does not directly execute the complete coupled transient described by the external model.

examples.title: Speaker transient identification with a copper shorting ring
examples.summary: Evaluate frequency/position maps for the source ring geometry, fit its L/R ladder using the stated exponential parameter curves, then compare external transient responses.
assumptions: The source samples explicit coil positions/frequencies and retains the ring placement.
limitations: Polynomial versus exponential parameter fits are different variants, not interchangeable without residual checks.
Ring effects depend on coil position.

examples.title: Uniform applied planar field using IABCs
examples.summary: Modify planar IABC shell coercivity and magnetization so a uniform background field coexists with the object reaction field of an open domain.
assumptions: The source uses the planar-circle demagnetization relation.
limitations: The corresponding spherical axisymmetric relation has a different factor.

examples.title: Uniform applied axial field using IABCs
examples.summary: Apply the source sphere-based shell magnetization prescription to generate a uniform axial field in an axisymmetric interior region.
assumptions: The source uses the sphere demagnetization relation and axial magnetization.
limitations: Planar and axisymmetric prescriptions cannot be substituted numerically.

examples.title: Square capacitor: quarter symmetry and charge extraction
examples.summary: Construct one quarter of the square-annulus capacitor, prescribe inner/outer conductor voltages and infer full-device capacitance from conductor charge.
assumptions: The dielectric is air and the source planar depth is explicit.
The quarter-model charge is scaled by four before computing full-device capacitance.
limitations: A symmetry factor must be tied to this geometry, not inherited by every capacitance calculation.

examples.title: Two-sphere capacitor: open boundary and electrostatic force
examples.summary: Represent the oppositely biased spheres with axisymmetric arcs and symmetry/open-boundary treatment, then obtain conductor charge and weighted-stress force.
assumptions: The source explicitly states sphere size, separation and equal/opposite potentials.
limitations: Grounding an artificial finite outer boundary changes charge/capacitance relative to the open-domain model.

examples.summary: Build a quarter square-annulus brick chimney, apply distinct inner/outer convection boundaries and integrate heat flux with the proper depth and symmetry scaling.
assumptions: The source has a planar depth and distinct ambient temperatures/film coefficients on inner and outer surfaces.
limitations: A prescribed-temperature boundary would be a different model from convection.
